text:
elena: quick FYI - customer reported accidental cross-tenant access because two different teams minted API keys with identical prefixes. Keys are parsed by prefix for routing and we ended up routing traffic to the wrong key registry in a multi-tenant on-prem config.

marc: ouch. example?

elena: Team A created key prefix 'svc-pay-'. Team B later created 'svc-pay-' in a different org. Our edge logic matches first prefix and picks the wrong tenant registry under a fallback path. Result: telemetry and request attribution mixed.

tom: that's a nasty combination of name-based routing + fallback semantics. Why are we relying on prefixes for tenant routing in the first place?

vik: legacy performance optimization. Edge nodes keep small prefix maps to route token introspection to local caches instead of full DB lookup. It's fast but brittle when prefixes collide and fallback is permissive.

elena: customer impact: billing, audits, and some RBAC checks used the routed registry to decide which tenant policies to apply. For a short window some read-only ops happened under the wrong tenant attribution.

marc: principle: routing keys must be canonical and collision-resistant. Proposals: 1) namespace keys with a stable issuer id (e.g., org short-hash) embedded in prefix; 2) switch to full token header with issuer id (no prefix parsing) and use prefix only as a cache hint; 3) deterministic tie-breaker rules with strict no-fallback for ambiguous matches.

tom: option 2 sounds safest long-term: require tokens to include issuer metadata as a top-level claim and have edges always prefer explicit issuer over prefix. Prefix remains hint only. Minimal infra change but requires token minting change across SDKs.

vik: option 1 low-lift: automatically rewrite new keys to include issuer: e.g., svc-pay@org-1_abc123-<rand>. That prevents future collisions but doesn't fix existing keys. We need migration for existing colliding prefixes.

elena: migration path idea: - detect prefixes that match multiple registries (scanner) - for conflicting prefixes, mark them "ambiguous" and force edge to call authoritative introspection endpoint instead of local route - contact owners to rotate to new structured prefix within 30 days - after TTL, treat ambiguous prefixes as invalid for routing (fail-open? fail-closed?).

marc: fail-closed for auth decisions, but fail-open for telemetry with a clear tag. In practice, auth must be conservative. So if prefix ambiguous and edge cannot fetch authoritative introspection, reject requests. We should provide a short-circuit emergency path for high-availability customers to opt into blocking vs allowing with strict audit.

tom: implementation details: 1) add scanner job that enumerates prefixes and detects overlaps (marc) 2) edge behavior change: if prefix matches multiple registries => disable cache-route and call /introspect?key_id=fulltoken instead (vik) 3) enforce token claim issuer required for new tokens minted (tom) 4) add migration CLI that helps owners rotate keys (elena)

security-bot: security-scan: found 14 ambiguous prefixes across hosted + dedicated clusters. https://ci.internal/scan/5098765432

vik: also think about attacks: an attacker could intentionally craft keys with colliding prefixes to force extra introspection load (DoS). So scanner should also rate-limit auto-resolve and the edge call should be authenticated and rate-limited per-prefix. Consider requiring signed prefix registration to accept fast-path routing.

marc: good catch. Signed prefix registration means the control-plane signs a small prefix registry entry {prefix, issuer, sig}. Edges accept fast-path only when signature present and signature verified. That prevents a rogue tenant from registering a prefix without control-plane attestation. For Private, operator signs their own prefix registry and can import it.

elena: next: policy language ramifications. Some policies 'resource.owner == key.prefix_owner' currently assume prefix_owner is authoritative. We should introduce explicit attribute key.issuer in policy language and deprecate prefix_owner. Add linter warnings for prefix_owner usage.

tom: sample policy change suggestion:
  // old
  allow if resource.owner == key.prefix_owner;
  // new
  allow if resource.owner == key.issuer;

marc: action items and owners: - prefix scanner + ambiguous report (marc) - edge fallback behavior & signed-registration verifier (vik) - token mint change to include issuer claim + SDK updates (tom) - key rotation CLI + customer comms (elena) - policy linter rule for prefix_owner -> key.issuer replacement (marc)

elena: timeline? customers affected want fix asap. Can we do scanner + edge fallback in 2 weeks and SDK token claim change in 3 weeks?

vik: yes for scanner + fallback (edge change needs careful rollout). Signed-registration in 4w. SDK and minting change 3w but we'll support dual-issuance: new tokens include issuer claim, old tokens still valid until rotate.

marc: add observability: metric auth_route_resolution{fastpath, authoritative, ambiguous, rejected} and a daily report for ambiguous prefixes owners list. Also emit audit tag when prefix fallback occurred. Create ticket AUTH-4802.

security-bot: created ticket AUTH-4802 for prefix collision work https://tickets.internal/AUTH-4802

elena: migration details for Private: operator can upload their signed prefix registry. We'll add a compatibility mode where edges trust operator-signed registry for fastpath. Document rotation and rollback steps.

tom: also update docs and SDK to prefer issuer-first validation. Add example: header 'X-Issuer: org-1' is optional but recommended for client libraries; however real verification must read signed claim inside token.

vik: final note: avoid relying on human-readable prefixes for authority. Use structured identifiers and signatures. This whole class of bugs comes from string matching heuristics.

elena: agreed. I'll draft the migration RFC and ping everyone for review. Please triage the scanner results and we'll contact affected customers before enforcement. Thanks! :thumbsup:
